mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 5 Series 518i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a BMW 5 Series 518i, a used M40B18 or M43B18 engine typically costs £300-£800 supply-only. Reconditioned units range from £900-£2,000, while a full rebuilt engine with warranty is £1,500-£3,000. Fitting adds approximately £400-£800 depending on the specialist.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 5 Series 518i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning is a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start, which subsides as oil pressure builds. As wear progresses, the rattle may persist when idling or under load.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 5 Series 518i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the car's overall condition and value. A clean, low-mileage E34 518i in good condition may justify a reconditioned or rebuilt engine. However, if the car is worth under £3,000 and needs a full engine replacement, it may be more economical to sell the car for parts and buy another example.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 5 Series 518i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 5 Series 518i engine replacement takes 2-3 days for a specialist workshop, including removal of the old engine, fitting the replacement unit and testing.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the M40B18 and M43B18 engines in the 518i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are 1.8-litre four-cylinder petrol engines, but the M43B18 (introduced April 1994) is an evolution of the M40 with improved fuel injection (Bosch Motronic 1.7.1 vs 1.3) and a slight power increase from 113hp to 115hp.

mainEntity.name: Can I upgrade my BMW 5 Series 518i to a larger engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: While it's technically possible to fit a 520i or 525i engine, it's rarely cost-effective. You would need the donor engine, engine loom, ECU, exhaust system and potentially the gearbox and rear axle. The 518i's M40/M43 engines are reliable and economical; a well-maintained example is often the better choice.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 5 Series 518i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 518i debuted in 1974 as the entry-level petrol variant of the first-generation 5 Series (E12), offering an affordable route into BMW executive saloon ownership. Over four generations, the 518i badge was powered by a succession of 1.8-litre four-cylinder petrol engines, each bringing incremental improvements in power, fuel efficiency and emissions compliance until the badge was retired with the E34 generation in 1996.

milestones.description: M10B18 (1.8L, 102hp) - power increase for the E12 518i.
M10B18 (1.8L, 105hp) - E28 generation 518i with Bosch K-Jetronic fuel injection.
M40B18 (1.8L, 113hp) - E34 518i launched August 1989 with Bosch Motronic DME M1.3.
M43B18 (1.8L, 115hp) - updated single-overhead-cam engine from April 1994 with Bosch Motronic 1.7.1.
End of production - BMW 518i discontinued; no direct 1.8-litre petrol successor in the 5 Series range.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 5 Series 518i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 5 Series 518i's M40 and M43 four-cylinder engines are among the more straightforward BMW powerplants to maintain, but age-related wear still catches many owners out. The most common replacement-demand drivers for the 518i are timing chain tensioner failure and oil leaks. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded timing chain tensioners and new gaskets addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the BMW 5 Series 518i M40/M43 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner relies on oil pressure and a spring mechanism. Over time, the tensioner loses effectiveness, allowing chain slack. If left unaddressed, chain slap can damage the timing chain guides or, in severe cases, cause the chain to jump teeth.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New tensioner, inspection of chain and guides
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early with rattle on cold start only

repairOptions.tier: Full timing chain kit (chain, guides, tensioner)
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if chain has stretched or guides are worn

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded tensioner and new gaskets, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the engine has jumped timing or internal damage is confirmed

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 5 Series 518i (E34) in fair-to-good condition is worth approximately £2,000-£7,000 depending on mileage and condition [THIRD-PARTY]. If your 518i is valued under £4,000, a timing chain repair (rather than a full engine replacement) is usually the more sensible financial decision. If the engine has already jumped timing causing internal damage, replacement cost may approach or exceed vehicle value - evaluate scrap value carefully before committing to a full rebuild on a sub-£3,000 example.
problems.recommendation: If you catch the timing chain rattle early, replacing just the tensioner is cost-effective and can extend engine life significantly. If the chain has stretched or guides are damaged, a full timing chain kit replacement is the prudent route. Only opt for a full rebuilt engine if the existing unit has suffered catastrophic timing failure or internal damage - the M40 and M43 engines are fundamentally robust and worth repairing where possible.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M40B18 / M43B18 BMW 5 Series 518i engine prices

problems.h4: Oil Leaks - Valve Cover and Timing Case Gaskets
problems.rootCause: Age-related perishing of rubber and cork gaskets. The valve cover gasket and timing case gasket are the most common leak points on the M40 and M43 engines.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New gasket, often requires timing cover removal
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for leaks from the front of the engine

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit with all new gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: Only if oil leaks have caused neglect or other issues

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a 518i valued under £4,000, gasket replacements are almost always worth doing. These are relatively low-cost repairs that can prevent oil loss and potential engine damage. Full engine replacement is rarely justified for oil leaks alone.
problems.recommendation: Replace gaskets as soon as leaks are noticed. Oil leaks left unattended can lead to low oil levels, which in turn can accelerate timing chain wear. This is preventative maintenance, not a reason to replace the engine.
